finding.claim: For MariaDB-classified servers the driver forces TLS rejectUnauthorized=false, overriding the user's setting, and sends credentials before any certificate-identity check. An on-path attacker who flips the plaintext greeting's MariaDB classification can receive the native-password scramble, and with caching_sha2_password under ssl receive the password in cleartext.
finding.source: Plaintext server greeting (on-path attacker controls it): lib/cmd/handshake/auth/initial-handshake.js:58-64 sets serverVersion.mariaDb from raw.includes('MariaDB') or from missing CLIENT_MYSQL bit (lib/const/capabilities.js:9 MYSQL=1n), or a '5.5.5-' prefix. Precondition: ssl enabled (default ssl:true, requireValidCert true) and attacker presents a cert failing CA/hostname verification.
finding.sink: Credential transmission before identity verification: lib/cmd/handshake/auth/handshake.js:134 native scramble written at handshake.js:156-159 via Handshake.send at handshake.js:77; caching-sha2 cleartext at lib/cmd/handshake/auth/caching-sha2-password-auth.js:60-66 (writeString(opts.password)) when opts.ssl is set.

trace.note: mariaDb flag derived from attacker-controllable greeting
Object.assign({}, this.opts.ssl, baseConf) - override wins over user rejectUnauthorized:true
tls.connect with unverified peer; Node sets socket.authorized=false on identity/CA failure but does not abort
selfSignedCertificate = !authorized, computed but not enforced here
only guard: requireValidCert && selfSigned && password && !isMitmProof(); isMitmProof() is false only for mysql_clear_password, so native and caching_sha2 pass
server replies fast-auth 0x04; if opts.ssl, cleartext password is written with no identity check
hostname/identity check (tls.checkServerIdentity) only runs after the OK packet, i.e. after credentials were sent

finding.guards_checked: requireValidCert computed (connection.js:1340-1343) but overridden for MariaDB; handshake.js:44 requireSecure for clear text only; handshake.js:54-56 SSL-capability check (blocks plaintext downgrade, not MITM); plugin-auth.js:38-40 isSecureConnection (satisfied by TLS); validateFingerPrint (authentication.js:215-244) only after OK packet; restrictedAuth (authentication.js:272). Not dynamically verified: needs a MITM test harness.

finding.claim: pool.escape() picks the escape mode from an arbitrary idle connection, and falls back to backslash escaping when none is available. On a server running NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES this yields SQL injection through escaped string values.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled string passed to pool.escape(value) (e.g. user input containing a backslash and a quote). Precondition: server sql_mode includes NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, and pool.escape() is called when no idle connection exists (all connections checked out, or the pool is cold).
finding.sink: Escaped literal interpolated into SQL by the application, executed on a session where backslash is ordinary text.

trace.note: active-connection scan iterates the Object.keys() array indices ('0','1',...), which never match numeric threadId keys, so it breaks with conn undefined
info stays null when no conn
noBackslashEscapes = info != null && ... => false when info is null
input \\' becomes \\\\\\' (backslash-mode escaping) which, under NO_BACKSLASH, ends the literal early

finding.guards_checked: utils.js:255 null guard (documented as intentional default); connection-level escape (connection.js:112) uses the connection's own info and is correct; escapeId unaffected. Exploit example: value \\' OR 1=1 -- -> SQL '\\\' OR 1=1 -- ' under NO_BACKSLASH. Not dynamically verified.

finding.claim: The big5 multibyte recognizer treats 0xFA-0xFE as lead bytes, which the server does not (server range 0xA1-0xF9, to be confirmed). A Buffer parameter containing [0xFA,0x5C,0x27] is therefore written as FA 5C 5C 27, where the server reads 5C 5C as an escaped backslash and the quote as bare, closing the literal.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled Buffer bound as a parameter (e.g. uploaded bytes). Precondition: connection charset big5 (e.g. charset 'BIG5_CHINESE_CI').
finding.sink: Query text sent to server: _BINARY '<bytes>' literal built by writeBufferEscape.
finding.guards_checked: String path is JS-level and safe (packet-output-stream.js:549-574); NO_BACKSLASH mode bypasses the mb walk safely (packet-output-stream.js:689); gbk/sjis/cp932/gb18030 recognizers match the server ranges as I read them; chunk-boundary corruption (packet-output-stream.js:677-682) is data corruption, not injection. Server range (0xA1-0xF9) is from memory and must be confirmed against a live big5 server, e.g. CHAR_LENGTH(_big5 X'FA5C') should be 1 if 0xFA is a lead byte.

finding.claim: A server-supplied redirect_url makes the driver open a new connection to a server-chosen host with the configured user and password, with no host allowlist. permitRedirect is on by default whenever ssl is set.
finding.source: Server-supplied redirect_url in session-state tracking of OK packets. Precondition: an authenticated server or proxy sends a redirect; default permitRedirect true when ssl is configured (connection-options.js:114-117).
finding.sink: Credential forwarding: new Connection with Object.assign({}, this.opts, redirectOpts), which carries the original password and user to the redirect target.

trace.note: gated on permitRedirect and single response, not in transaction (2076)
new ConnOptions with original opts (password/user) -> connect()

finding.guards_checked: protocol scheme check (2084); same-host loop check (2099); transaction and pipelining gating (2076); TLS identity check applies to the new host but is subject to the F1 MariaDB override. No host allowlist or per-redirect credential control. Likely by design (proxy/MaxScale routing); impact requires a compromised or malicious server.

finding.claim: changeUser() overwrites the connection's stored password with the new one but leaves the stored user unchanged. Later automatic reconnects or redirects therefore authenticate as the old user with the new user's password, which is an inconsistent identity and a source of failures.
finding.sink: Stored connection options used for later reconnect/redirect authentication.

trace.note: connOpts.password = cmdOpts.password (mutates the shared connection options; user not updated)

finding.guards_checked: Server still enforces credentials, so no bypass found; undefined password from changeUser also overwrites stored password. Note: I did not verify the call site that passes connOpts into ChangeUser; impact is logic/availability, low.

finding.claim: With allowPublicKeyRetrieval enabled and no TLS, the RSA public key is taken from the server without fingerprint pinning, so an on-path attacker can substitute a key and recover the password encrypted with it.
finding.source: Server-supplied public key packet (on-path attacker). Precondition: allowPublicKeyRetrieval:true, ssl not enabled, and no rsaPublicKey/cachingRsaPublicKey configured.
finding.sink: crypto.publicEncrypt of the XOR'd password (sha256-password-auth.js:98, 137; caching-sha2-password-auth.js:107-109).

trace.note: TLS path sends cleartext over TLS instead (preferred when ssl)
opt-in check, else request key from server

finding.guards_checked: Explicit opt-in flag (default false); rsaPublicKey / cachingRsaPublicKey preferred when set (sha256 line 47); TLS path preferred. Documented trade-off, so low severity; the risk is in unpinned TOFU when the option is enabled on untrusted networks.
